microtheory.name: reflection_metaprogramming
microtheory.definition: Reflection — system's ability to observe + modify itself from within. Brian Cantwell Smith 1982 'Reflection and Semantics in Lisp', the reflective tower, Smalltalk's metaobject protocol, Lisp's eval/quote, Java reflection, metaprogramming, self-modifying code, Quine, fixed-point combinators. Directly grounds Paper 1's Axiom 3 (Reflective access): Π operations observe, predicate over, and extend G from within G. G's own structure including Γ itself is representable as subgraph of G. This Mt names the existing tradition of reflection that Axiom 3 generalises to the substrate level.

concepts.name: reflection_definition
concepts.definition: Smith 1982. System's capacity to observe + reason about + modify its own structure + behavior from within itself. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's introspection.

concepts.name: structural_reflection
concepts.definition: Access to representation of system's structure (types, classes, methods, AST). Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's typed-graph + Γ as graph data.

concepts.name: behavioral_reflection
concepts.definition: Ability to modify system's behavior (intercept method calls, change dispatch). Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's runtime-discovery dispatch.

concepts.name: introspection
concepts.definition: Read-only reflection. System observes itself without modifying. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's derivation_mechanism.

concepts.name: intercession
concepts.definition: Read-write reflection. System modifies own behavior. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's correction-firing + self-modification.

concepts.name: reflective_tower
concepts.definition: Smith. Infinite hierarchy of meta-levels, each interpreting the level below. Stack of interpreters interpreting interpreters. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's nested cortices (Mt about Mts about Mts).

concepts.name: meta_level
concepts.definition: Level above the base level, reasoning about it. Each meta-level can be reflected on by the next. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's ArchitectureCortex assessing other cortices.

concepts.name: base_level
concepts.definition: Object-level computation. The thing being reflected upon. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's per-Mt processing.

concepts.name: tower_collapse
concepts.definition: Practical tower truncated at finite depth via lazy materialisation. Smith's design. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's bounded meta-cognition.

concepts.name: metaobject_protocol
concepts.definition: MOP. Kiczales + Rivières + Bobrow 1991 (CLOS). Reify language semantics into objects manipulable from within. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's seed-system as metaobjects.

concepts.name: metaclass
concepts.definition: Class whose instances are themselves classes. Substrate analogue: Mt that defines other Mts.

concepts.name: reflective_method_dispatch
concepts.definition: Intercept + modify how methods are called. Aspect-oriented programming. Substrate analogue: substrate's FilterSpec dispatch interception.

concepts.name: lisp_eval_quote
concepts.definition: McCarthy 1960. eval reduces expression; quote suspends evaluation. Code-as-data + data-as-code. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's Term-tree representation + evaluation.

concepts.name: homoiconicity
concepts.definition: Code + data share representation. Lisp's defining feature. Foundation of macro systems. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's graph holds both data + computation.

concepts.name: macro_lisp
concepts.definition: Code that generates code. Operates at expansion time. Hygienic macros avoid variable capture. Substrate analogue: substrate's mechanical Term-emitters.

concepts.name: fexpr
concepts.definition: First-class operative — takes unevaluated args. Suspended eval. Substrate analogue: substrate's deferred Term-evaluation.

concepts.name: self_modifying_code
concepts.definition: Program writes to own instruction stream. Historically common in assembly; now mostly avoided for security + caching. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's self-modification at meta-level not instruction level.

concepts.name: runtime_compilation
concepts.definition: Generate + execute code at runtime. JIT. Substrate analogue: substrate's runtime-generated handlers.

concepts.name: code_as_data_data_as_code
concepts.definition: Symmetric: parsable + executable representations. Foundation of metaprogramming. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's typed-graph IS this symmetry.

concepts.name: quine_program
concepts.definition: Self-replicating program. Outputs its own source. Substrate analogue: substrate's persist-self capability.

concepts.name: fixed_point_combinator
concepts.definition: Y combinator etc. Enables recursion in untyped lambda calculus without explicit recursion. Substrate analogue: substrate's recursive self-application.

concepts.name: diagonal_lemma
concepts.definition: Gödel. For every formula φ(x), there exists sentence ψ such that ψ ↔ φ(⌜ψ⌝). Self-reference machinery. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-referential Mt-construction.

concepts.name: godel_numbering_reflection
concepts.definition: Encode syntax as numbers. Reflective access through arithmetisation. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's symbol-as-node encoding.

concepts.name: java_reflection_api
concepts.definition: Class, Method, Field reified at runtime. Access by name. Substrate analogue: substrate's name-based node access.

concepts.name: smalltalk_reflective
concepts.definition: Smalltalk-80 — everything an object including classes. Pure object-oriented + reflective. Substrate analogue: substrate's uniform-typed graph.

concepts.name: python_introspection
concepts.definition: dir(), vars(), getattr(), inspect module. Pervasive runtime reflection. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective access patterns.

concepts.name: grammar_as_data
concepts.definition: The Γ in Paper 1 Axiom 3 is representable AS a subgraph of G. Same as Lisp's homoiconicity at the grammar level. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's Γ-as-graph-node.

concepts.name: operations_on_grammar
concepts.definition: Once Γ is graph data, operations in Π can operate on Γ itself. Self-modifying grammar. Substrate analogue: substrate's seed-Mt evolution.

concepts.name: compound_loop_axiom3
concepts.definition: Paper 1 §2.1: a Γ that admits operations on itself IS a compound loop. A Γ that does not is inert. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's loop-by-self-modification.

concepts.name: frame_problem_reflection
concepts.definition: McCarthy + Hayes 1969. What does NOT change when X happens? Requires reflection over situation. Substrate analogue: substrate's preserved-Mt under correction.

concepts.name: russells_paradox_reflection
concepts.definition: Self-applying naive reflection produces contradictions. Solved by typed hierarchy, restricted comprehension. Substrate analogue: substrate's typed-graph as guard.

concepts.name: self_replication_constraints
concepts.definition: Reflection limited by physical resource bounds + halting problem. Substrate analogue: substrate's bounded reflection.

rules.name: reflection_grounds_paper1_axiom3
rules.head: Jabberwock encounters Paper 1's Axiom 3 (Reflective access)
rules.body: the axiom generalises Smith's reflection + Lisp's homoiconicity + metaobject protocols to the substrate level. Γ-as-subgraph IS homoiconicity at the grammar layer. Operations on Γ from within Γ IS Smith's reflective tower one level up.

rules.name: homoiconicity_enables_grammar_operations
rules.head: Jabberwock represents grammar Γ as graph data
rules.body: operations in Π can operate on Γ — substrate's grammar becomes a variable. Paper 1's §2.1 'the grammar is the loop' is homoiconicity applied to Γ.

rules.name: reflective_tower_models_meta_cognition
rules.head: Jabberwock holds Mts that reason about Mts
rules.body: this is the reflective tower. Each level reflects on the level below. Smith's design lets the tower be finite-depth in practice via lazy materialisation.

rules.name: introspection_is_read_only_reflection
rules.head: Jabberwock's derivation_mechanism walks its own state
rules.body: this is introspection (read-only reflection). Modification of state would be intercession. Substrate's self-modification spans both.

rules.name: fixed_point_grounds_recursion_without_naming
rules.head: Jabberwock needs recursion without external naming
rules.body: Y combinator + diagonal lemma provide the mathematical machinery. Substrate's recursive Mt-construction relies on this.
